A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 26-page DiffWind study, including Appendices A–F. Text, equations, tables, figures, and embedded animation resources support reliable comparison; differences are confined to bibliography presentation and the arXiv version stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments, ablations, forward simulations, and a 32-participant user study in Section 4, with additional results in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including reconstruction scores, simulation evaluations, ablations, the user study, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 and the appendices retain identical Gaussian/MPM interaction modeling, wind-force optimization, LBM guidance, segmentation, and invisible-point densification procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same seven synthetic and four real-world reconstruction scenes, four forward-simulation scenes, and wind-retargeting scenarios in Sections 4.2–4.4 and Appendix E.

E2.justification: The reconstruction comparators remain Deformable-GS, Efficient-GS, 4D-GS, and GaussianPrediction. The video-generation comparator set is also unchanged, and both versions retain the PhysDreamer and PhysFlow comparisons in Appendix E.2.

E3.justification: Both retain the same synthetic four-view training/four-view testing split, 50 evaluation timesteps, PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS metrics, baseline initialization controls, and 32-participant rating protocol. No experimental settings are revised.

E4.justification: The physics-informed-loss, material-property, densification, and grid-resolution ablations in Tables 3–6 are identical. Appendix E retains the same qualitative densification examples and computational scalability analyses.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version adds repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests; the same point estimates and user-study averages are reported.

E6.justification: Tables 1–9 and the qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, synthetic average PSNR remains 47.15 in Table 1, the average user-study score remains 4.34 in Table 7, and average wind-field cosine similarity remains 0.9249 in Table 9.

T1.justification: Equations 1–26, the physical assumptions and background mathematics in Appendix A, and the segmentation and HOME-LBM formulations in Appendices B and D are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning joint wind/object reconstruction, physics-informed constraints, novel-wind simulation, retargeting, WD-Objects, and superiority over prior methods.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and applicability boundaries are unchanged, including the material/force identifiability discussion, multi-object collision limitations in Section 5, turbulence limitations in Appendix A.2, and computational tradeoffs in Appendix E.3.

D1.justification: Training settings, Taichi implementation, RTX 4090 hardware, timing and memory information, and appendix prompt templates are unchanged. The project URL and statement promising source-code release upon acceptance also remain the same.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Bibliography edits expand venue abbreviations such as 'Proc. of CVPR' and 'ACM TOG'; they do not introduce different references or revise relationships to prior work.

P1.justification: Bibliography wording expands abbreviated venue names and removes the duplicated 'In' in the Neuma reference. The arXiv version/date stamp changes, while the scientific prose, section structure, and appendix wording remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Longer bibliography entries reflow across pages 11–14; for example, the Detector-free structure from motion reference moves from page 11 to page 12. Figures, tables, and the layout of the scientific body and appendices are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 provides modest bibliography polish through expanded venue names and a duplicated-word correction, with accompanying reference reflow. The scientific exposition, empirical evidence, technical guidance, and limitations remain identical, so these cosmetic edits do not meaningfully change overall paper quality.
